Strangers in foreign colours stand about in the middle of <name>, and the locals walk around them as if they were furniture nobody wanted. The forges of <name> are quiet more often than not, for want of iron. Guests are greeted with a cup before a word of business is spoken.
War has taken the iron: the metal suppliers sell to the armies first, and the smiths have nothing to mend tools with. Work slows, and people are starting to complain.
